title: Stiefel Whitney and Euler Classes by Universal Constructions

items.title: Characteristic class as a universal natural bundle class
items.statement: Assume AC and work with numerable rank-n bundles over paracompact Hausdorff CGWH bases. A degree-k characteristic class over R is an isomorphism-invariant, pullback-natural assignment E↦c(E)∈H^k(B;R). For real, complex, or oriented real bundles this is equivalently a class of the tautological bundle on BO(n), BU(n), or BSO(n), pulled back along any classifying map.
items.proof_plan: Evaluate a natural assignment on the universal bundle. Conversely pull back a fixed universal class; homotopy invariance and the published classification theorem give independence and naturality. Include rank zero and components. AC is inherited only from classification.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; AC is used through numerable-bundle classification.

references.title: Haynes Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II

items.title: Totals of numerable bundles with compact fibre are paracompact Hausdorff of CW type
items.statement: Assume AC. A numerable locally trivial fiber bundle with compact Hausdorff fibre over a paracompact Hausdorff base has paracompact Hausdorff total space; if base and fibre have the homotopy type of CW complexes then so does the total space. Consequently projective and flag bundles of compact-fibre numerable bundles over such bases, and their finite fiber products over the base, are again paracompact Hausdorff of CW type.
items.proof_plan: Hausdorff by local product charts; paracompact by the tube lemma applied fiberwise with a locally finite refinement of the base cover; CW type by Schon Theorem 2 for the Hurewicz fibration.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC (finite subcover choices for the paracompactness argument).

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Vector Bundles & K-Theory
references.locator: §3.1 projective bundles over paracompact bases, printed pp.77–78

references.title: Rolf Schon, Fibrations Over a CWh-Base

items.title: Real projective bundle and tautological line
items.statement: For a rank-n real vector bundle E→B, n≥1, P(E)→B has fiber P(E_b)≅RP^{n-1}; its tautological line gamma_E has fiber L over (b,L). Bundle transitions induce both bundles. For n=0 set P(E)=∅.
items.proof_plan: Glue U_i×RP^{n-1} by the projectivized transition cocycle and glue the selected lines by its linear action. Check the cocycle and empty rank-zero convention.

references.title: Haynes Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II

items.title: Tautological degree-one class on a real projective bundle
items.statement: Assume AC. For n≥1 choose a classifying map c_{gamma_E}:P(E)→BO(1)=RP^∞ for gamma_E and let a∈H^1(RP^∞;F_2) be the fixed generator. Define x_E=c_{gamma_E}^*a. This does not use w_1.
items.proof_plan: Define through the published classifying-map interface, leaving independence and fiber normalization to the following lemma; do not invoke Stiefel–Whitney classes.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; AC is inherited from classifying-map existence.

items.title: The tautological degree-one class is well defined and fiber generating
items.statement: Assume AC. The class x_E is independent of the classifying map. On every fiber RP^{n-1} it restricts to the standard degree-one generator (zero for n=1), so 1,x_E,…,x_E^{n-1} restrict to the standard cohomology basis.
items.proof_plan: Classification uniqueness makes two classifying maps homotopic, hence their pullbacks agree. A fiber restriction classifies its tautological line and is homotopic to RP^{n-1}→RP^∞; use the published skeletal polynomial calculation, including n=1.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; AC occurs through classification.

items.title: Mod-two real projective bundle theorem
items.statement: Assume AC. For a numerable real rank-n bundle E, n≥1, over a CW complex, H^*(P(E);F_2) is free over H^*(B;F_2) on 1,x,…,x^{n-1}. There are unique c_i(E)∈H^i(B;F_2) with x^n+c_1x^{n-1}+⋯+c_n=0, and this monic relation generates all polynomial relations.
items.proof_plan: Apply Leray–Hirsch only after the preceding fiber-basis lemma, componentwise if needed. Expand x^n uniquely; grading locates each coefficient. Monic division gives normal forms and module-basis uniqueness proves the relation ideal claim.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; AC is inherited from classification and Leray–Hirsch.

references.title: Haynes Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II

items.title: Stiefel–Whitney classes from the projective-bundle relation
items.statement: Assume AC. Define w_i(E) by x^n+w_1(E)x^{n-1}+⋯+w_n(E)=0, set w_0=1 and w_i=0 above rank, and write w(E)=Σw_i(E). For a line L, P(L)≅B and the relation identifies x_L=w_1(L).
items.proof_plan: Adopt the unique projective-bundle coefficients and state the rank and total-class conventions. In rank one use characteristic two and P(L)≅B.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; inherited from the projective-bundle theorem.

references.title: Haynes Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II

items.title: Naturality of Stiefel–Whitney classes
items.statement: Assume AC. For every admissible base map f, w_i(f^*E)=f^*w_i(E) for all i and w(f^*E)=f^*w(E). The classes depend only on the bundle isomorphism class.
items.proof_plan: The pullback square of projective bundles pulls x_E back to x_{f^*E}. Pull back the monic relation and use uniqueness of its coefficients; specialize to isomorphisms over the identity.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; inherited from the projective-bundle definition of the classes.

items.title: Real flag bundle and Stiefel–Whitney roots
items.statement: Assume AC. Iteratively projectivize E, split off each tautological line using a bundle metric, and call the composite q:Fl(E)→B the real flag bundle. Then q^*E≅L_1⊕⋯⊕L_n; t_j=w_1(L_j) are its roots. For n=0, Fl(E)=B and the sum is empty.
items.proof_plan: At each finite stage pull back a metric and take the orthogonal complement of the tautological line. Iterate the canonical splittings and define roots only after line w_1 exists.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; AC supplies the published bundle metric.

references.title: Haynes Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II

items.title: Real splitting principle with mod-two injective pullback
items.statement: Assume AC. The pullback q^*:H^*(B;F_2)→H^*(Fl(E);F_2) is injective and q^*E splits into lines. Finitely many bundles admit a common such splitting space with injective pullback.
items.proof_plan: Each projective-bundle pullback is inclusion of the coefficient-of-1 Leray–Hirsch summand, hence injective; compose them. For finitely many bundles iterate their flag constructions after pullback.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; inherited from projective-bundle and metric suppliers.

references.title: Haynes Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II

items.title: Whitney sum formula for Stiefel–Whitney classes
items.statement: Assume AC. For real bundles E,F, w(E⊕F)=w(E)w(F), equivalently w_k(E⊕F)=Σ_{i+j=k}w_i(E)w_j(F). Thus w(0)=1 and adjoining a trivial summand changes no positive class.
items.proof_plan: In P(E⊕F), form the two polynomials omega_E and omega_F given by the defining relations. They restrict to zero on P(E) and P(F), so lift to relative classes for complements that deformation retract to the opposite projective subbundles. Since P(E) and P(F) are disjoint, the relative cup product lands in the relative group for a cover of the whole space and is zero absolutely. Thus omega_E omega_F is the monic defining relation for E⊕F, and uniqueness gives the convolution formula. Check zero/trivial ranks; the already-built splitting principle is then available for later consumers.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; inherited from the splitting principle.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Vector Bundles & K-Theory
references.locator: Theorem 3.1 and splitting proof, printed pp.79–83

references.title: Haynes Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II

items.title: Uniqueness of Stiefel–Whitney classes from normalization, naturality, and sum
items.statement: Assume AC. The total Stiefel–Whitney class is the unique pullback-natural Whitney-multiplicative rule with degree-zero part 1 and W(gamma^1)=1+a for the universal line on RP^∞.
items.proof_plan: Pull any bundle to its flag bundle. Naturality, normalization, and multiplicativity force ∏(1+t_i), which is also the pullback of w(E). Injectivity forces equality on the base; include rank zero and components.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; inherited from splitting.

items.title: Mod-two cohomology of BO(n)
items.statement: Assume AC. For n≥0, H^*(BO(n);F_2)=F_2[w_1,…,w_n], with |w_i|=i; for n=0 this is F_2.
items.proof_plan: Induct on n with the unit-sphere bundle of gamma_n. Its total space is homotopy equivalent to BO(n-1) by orthogonal complement, with contractible stable-sphere fiber. Restriction sends w_j to w_j for j<n and w_n to zero, hence is onto. Gysin breaks into short exact sequences. Its mod-two Euler generator equals w_n: both span the degree-n kernel, and w_n is nonzero after pulling gamma_n back along RP^∞→BO(n) as n copies of the universal line, where it becomes a^n. Induct also on degree to obtain unique polynomial expansions.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; inherited from Gysin and the universal-bundle suppliers.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Vector Bundles & K-Theory
references.locator: Theorem 3.9 and Gysin proof, printed pp.85–90

references.title: Haynes Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II

items.title: The first Stiefel–Whitney class classifies orientability
items.statement: Assume AC. Real line bundles over the page's CW/paracompact base are naturally classified by H^1(B;F_2) through L↦w_1(L), and tensor product corresponds to addition. For every real bundle E, w_1(E)=0 iff E is orientable, equivalently its structure group reduces to SO(n).
items.proof_plan: BO(1)=RP^∞ is K(F_2,1) because its universal stable-sphere cover is contractible; combine bundle classification and cohomology representability. Transition signs show tensor additivity. The determinant line has the orientation-cover sign cocycle, while splitting and Whitney give w_1(det E)=w_1(E). It is trivial exactly when the orientation cover has a section; invoke the published SO-reduction equivalence.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; inherited from classification, representability, and splitting.

references.title: Haynes Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II

items.title: Euler class by zero-section pullback of the Thom class
items.statement: Assume AC, as in the general Thom theorem. For an R-oriented rank-n bundle E with normalized Thom class u_E, define e(E)=e_Th(E)=s^*j^*u_E∈H^n(B;R), where j^* is relative-to-absolute and s is the zero section. Thus the shorthand s^*u_E includes j^*. For rank zero e(0_B)=1.
items.proof_plan: Adopt the already published Thom-defined Euler class as this page's notation, fixing the typed map and rank-zero convention without creating a second construction.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC for general Thom-class existence; choice-free once u_E is supplied.

references.title: Haynes Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II

items.title: Naturality, orientation sign, and Whitney product for Euler classes
items.statement: Assume AC. Orientation-preserving pullback satisfies e(f^*E)=f^*e(E); reversing orientation negates e; and ordered product orientations give e(E⊕F)=e(E)e(F), including rank-zero units. Swapping ranks n,m carries the corresponding (-1)^{nm} orientation sign.
items.proof_plan: Use Thom-class naturality and the zero-section square for pullbacks, the orientation-reversal rule before j^* and s^*, and the published Thom Whitney-product formula followed by relative-to-absolute and zero-section pullback. Retain the ordered-product sign.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; inherited from Thom existence and uniqueness.

references.title: Haynes Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II

items.title: The mod-two Euler class is the top Stiefel–Whitney class
items.statement: Assume AC. For a real rank-n bundle E with canonical F_2-orientation, e_2(E)=w_n(E). If E is integrally oriented, rho_2(e(E))=w_n(E). Rank zero gives 1=1.
items.proof_plan: Pull to the flag bundle. For a line, the projective relation and Thom self-intersection identify e_2(L)=w_1(L). Euler and Whitney multiplicativity make both classes t_1⋯t_n after splitting; descend by injectivity. Coefficient naturality of normalized Thom classes gives the integral-reduction clause.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; inherited from splitting and Thom classes.

references.title: Haynes Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II

items.title: A nowhere-zero section forces the Euler class to vanish
items.statement: Assume AC. If an R-oriented positive-rank real bundle admits a nowhere-zero section, then e(E)=0. No converse is asserted.
items.proof_plan: Normalize the section into S(E). It splits the sphere projection, so inclusion S(E)→D(E) induces an injection in cohomology. Exactness forces the relative-to-absolute map to vanish; hence s^*j^*u_E=0. Positive rank excludes e(0)=1.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC only through Thom-class existence.

items.title: The Euler class of an oriented odd-rank bundle is two-torsion
items.statement: Assume AC. For an integrally oriented real bundle (E,o) of odd positive rank, 2e(E,o)=0. Unconditional vanishing is not asserted.
items.proof_plan: Since det(-I)=-1, -id is orientation-preserving as (E,o)→(E,-o). Oriented naturality over id gives e(E,o)=e(E,-o), while the orientation-sign law gives e(E,-o)=-e(E,o). Combine them. Do not claim -id is homotopic to id.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC only through the Euler/Thom supplier.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Vector Bundles & K-Theory
references.locator: Euler orientation sign and Proposition 3.13(d), printed pp.90–92; proof route follows binding owner direction

items.title: Thom identity for Stiefel–Whitney classes
items.statement: Assume AC. For the normalized mod-two Thom class u_E of a real rank-n bundle, Sq(u_E)=w(E)u_E; equivalently Sq^i(u_E)=w_i(E)u_E and the terms above rank vanish.
items.proof_plan: For a line, instability and the top-square law give Sq(u)=u+u^2, while Thom self-intersection gives u^2=e_2(L)u=w_1(L)u. Pull E to its flag bundle, use the Thom product and Cartan formulas to get ∏(1+t_i)u, and identify this with w(q^*E)u. Naturality, injectivity on base, and the Thom isomorphism descend the identity; include rank zero.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; inherited from Thom, Steenrod, and splitting suppliers.

references.title: Haynes Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II

items.title: The quaternion double cover generates the third homotopy group of SO(3)
items.statement: The conjugation action of the unit quaternions makes S^3 the group Sp(1) of unit quaternions and defines a continuous surjective two-sheeted covering homomorphism rho:S^3->SO(3) with kernel {+1,-1}, rho(q)(v)=qvq^{-1}. Covering projections induce isomorphisms on pi_n for n>=2, so rho_*:pi_3(S^3,1)->pi_3(SO(3),I) is an isomorphism; pi_3(S^3,1) is Z by degree, hence pi_3(SO(3),I) is Z generated by the class [rho]; and the clutching construction over the equatorial S^3 produces a nontrivial oriented rank-three real vector bundle E_rho->S^4.
items.proof_plan: Prove (xy)bar = ybar xbar and N(xy)=N(x)N(y), then expand conjugation by a unit quaternion q=a+r in the orthonormal basis (u,w,uw) to get qwqbar=(a^2-s^2)w+2as(uw), q(uw)qbar=(a^2-s^2)uw-2as w and quqbar=u. Deduce norm preservation, orthogonality and determinant one, so rho maps into SO(3) and is a continuous group homomorphism with kernel {+1,-1}; a nonidentity R in SO(3) has det(R-I)=0, hence a fixed unit vector, and its plane action is pinned down by the Leibniz determinant, which gives surjectivity. The {+1,-1} action is a covering-space action, so rho factors through a homeomorphism S^3/{+1,-1}->SO(3) and is a two-sheeted covering. Prove the pi_n isomorphism for n>=2 by homotopy lifting for injectivity and the lifting criterion with connected cube boundary for surjectivity; conclude pi_3(SO(3),I) is generated by [rho] via the degree isomorphism; rule out a nullhomotopy of rho by lifting it to a nullhomotopy of the identity of S^3; and make the clutched bundle E_rho nontrivial because constant clutching maps give the trivial bundle.
items.axiom_strength: ZF; no choice principle is used.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: §1.3, printed p.75 (unit quaternions and the two-to-one cover S^3 to SO(3)); §4.1, Proposition 4.1, printed p.342 (covering projections induce isomorphisms on pi_n for n at least 2); §4.2, Corollary 4.25, printed p.361 (pi_n(S^n) is Z, generated by the identity, via degree)

title: Stiefel Whitney and Euler Classes by Universal Constructions — Examples

items.title: Stiefel–Whitney class of the universal real line
items.statement: Assume AC. For the universal real line gamma^1→RP^∞, w(gamma^1)=1+a, where a generates H^1(RP^∞;F_2).
items.proof_plan: P(gamma^1)≅RP^∞ and its tautological line is gamma^1, so the rank-one projective relation is x+w_1=0. Here x=a and signs vanish over F_2; higher classes vanish by rank.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; inherited from the projective-bundle definition of the classes.

items.title: Total Stiefel–Whitney class of a sum of universal lines
items.statement: Assume AC. On (RP^∞)^n let L_i be the pullback of the universal line and a_i=w_1(L_i). Then H^*=F_2[a_1,…,a_n] and w(⊕L_i)=∏(1+a_i), so w_k is the k-th elementary symmetric polynomial.
items.proof_plan: Apply finite Künneth to the published polynomial calculation, identify the pullback generators, apply Whitney multiplicativity, and expand. Include n=0.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; inherited from Künneth and Whitney multiplicativity.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Vector Bundles & K-Theory
references.locator: Examples after the Whitney theorem, printed pp.82–83

references.title: Haynes Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II

items.title: Euler class of the universal oriented two-plane
items.statement: Assume AC. Under BSO(2)≃CP^∞ and the standard complex orientation, the Euler class of the universal oriented real two-plane is the chosen generator of H^2(BSO(2);Z)≅Z; its mod-two reduction is w_2.
items.proof_plan: Identify SO(2) with S^1 and BSO(2) with CP^∞. The universal unit-circle bundle has contractible total space, so Gysin makes multiplication by e an isomorphism H^0→H^2; the complex orientation fixes the sign. Then reduce mod two.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; inherited from classification and Gysin.

references.title: Haynes Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II

items.title: Euler class of zero and trivial positive-rank bundles
items.statement: Assume AC. For every base B, e(0_B)=1∈H^0(B;R), whereas every oriented trivial bundle epsilon_B^n of positive rank has Euler class zero.
items.proof_plan: The first value is the rank-zero convention. For n>0 use the constant first-basis-vector section and the vanishing proposition; include empty base and zero ring.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; inherited from general Thom-class existence.

items.title: Zero Euler class does not in general imply a nowhere-zero section
items.statement: Assume AC. There is an oriented rank-three real bundle E→S^4 with e(E)=0 but no nowhere-zero section.
items.proof_plan: Clutch by rho:S^3→SO(3), the quaternion double cover of the unit quaternions. A nullhomotopy would lift from id_{S^3} to a homotopy ending in a discrete fiber, contradicting degree one, so the bundle is nontrivial. Since H^3(S^4;Z)=0, e=0. A nonzero section would split E=epsilon^1⊕F with oriented rank-two F. Its S^3→SO(2)≅S^1 clutching map lifts to R and is null, making E trivial, contradiction.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; AC is inherited from UCT and the published bundle-splitting supplier.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Vector Bundles & K-Theory
references.locator: §1.2 clutching, printed pp.25–27; §3.3 Euler as primary obstruction, printed pp.98–106

items.title: An odd-rank Euler class need not vanish in the presence of two-torsion
items.statement: Assume AC. On B=RP^∞×RP^∞ there is an oriented real rank-three bundle whose integral Euler class is nonzero of order two.
items.proof_plan: Let a,b generate H^1(B;F_2), choose lines L_a,L_b,L_{a+b}, and set E=L_a⊕L_b⊕L_{a+b}. Then w_1(E)=0, so E is orientable, while w_3(E)=ab(a+b) is nonzero in F_2[a,b]. Thus rho_2e(E)=w_3(E) makes e nonzero, and the odd-rank proposition gives 2e=0.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + AC; inherited from line classification, Künneth, and Thom classes.
